plants.name: Cyclamen hederifolium
plants.description: Small swept-back pink petals rise on slender stems straight from the woodland floor. Each flower has a darker magenta blush at its base. Silver-marbled, ivy-shaped leaves follow and carpet the ground through winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Woodlands and rocky slopes of southern Europe and the northern Mediterranean, and in shady gardens across temperate Europe and North America
plants.funFact: After pollination, the flower stalk coils like a spring and pulls the seed capsule down to the soil. Ants then carry the sticky seeds away and spread the plant.

plants.name: Sternbergia lutea
plants.description: Glossy, golden-yellow goblets open on bare ground as the summer heat fades. They look like crocuses but are really autumn-flowering relatives of the daffodil. Strap-like leaves appear alongside the flowers or just after.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn, usually September
plants.location: Rocky hillsides, olive groves and scrubland from the western Mediterranean east to Central Asia
plants.funFact: Many botanists think this is the 'lily of the field' mentioned in ancient texts. It flowers best after a hot, dry summer bakes its bulbs.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Goblet-shaped lilac-pink flowers burst from the soil with no leaves in sight, which gives them the nickname 'naked ladies'. They scatter damp autumn meadows and woodland edges with soft colour. The broad green leaves appear only the following spring.
plants.location: Damp meadows and open woods across Europe, and in gardens in cooler temperate zones worldwide
plants.funFact: Every part of the plant is highly toxic. It is also the natural source of colchicine, a compound used in medicine and in plant breeding.
